items.title: Review: US Strikes Iranian Missile Site after Bahrain Attacks
items.summary: Bloomberg’s Jon Herskovitz discusses the latest exchange of strikes between the US and Iran after American warplanes hit an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps missile launch site in Iran. Iran previously targeted an air base in Bahrain in the first direct strike on the Gulf state in weeks, even as it reiterated that a path to ending the conflict with the US remains open. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Review: Anthropic Crypto Bets Imply $1.7 Trillion Value Despite AI Rout
items.summary: Crypto futures tied to Anthropic’s stock market debut have fallen alongside artificial intelligence stocks, but they still imply a blockbuster valuation of about $1.7 trillion, well above the $1.4 trillion the company would be worth at the top of its proposed initial public offering range.

items.title: Review: Trump Administration Presses Ahead in Legal Battle Over U.S. Attorneys
items.summary: A judge has ruled that Bill Essayli was acting “unlawfully” as U.S. attorney in Los Angeles. He is one of three prosecutors appointed by the Trump administration through a unique process.

items.title: Review: These Villagers Wonder if They’re on the Front Line of Russia’s Shadow War
items.summary: Russia is accused of clandestine attacks on Ukraine’s allies in Europe, most notably at Leipzig/Halle airport in eastern Germany. That has changed life for villagers nearby.

items.title: Review: Japan Attempts to Revive U.S. Steel
items.summary: After its fraught takeover of steel maker U.S. Steel, a Japanese manufacturer is attempting to revitalize the American company’s facilities, including its oldest mill outside Pittsburgh.

items.title: Review: Xi Pitches China as Open Ahead of Trump Meeting
items.summary: Bloomberg North Asia correspondent Minmin Low says Xi Jinping’s speech at the APEC CEO Summit offered few surprises, emphasizing China’s stability, openness and credentials as a testing ground for frontier technologies. Xi also touted the resilience of the Chinese economy, saying China would continue to stimulate domestic demand. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Review: Democrats Claim 56 Senate Seats After Mary Peltola Wins in Alaska
items.summary: Ms. Peltola defeated Senator Dan S. Sullivan, a two-term incumbent, to become the first Democrat to represent the conservative state in the Senate since 2015.

items.title: Review: Rubio Says Rush to Secure Systems May Be Causing Failures
items.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio suggested the rush to patch systems, whose vulnerabilities are exposed by A.I., may explain recent failures with air traffic controls, banks and government agencies.

items.title: Review: For Democrats, a Leadership Fight Is Marring an Electoral Triumph
items.summary: The contest between Senators Chuck Schumer and Chris Van Hollen to be majority leader is sowing party divisions and putting them on public display.

items.title: Review: Trump Asia trip live updates: Trump greets Philippines' president ahead of meeting
items.summary: Trump is scheduled this week to participate in the first-ever trilateral meeting with Putin and Xi.

items.title: Review: Asics Steps Up China Push With Goal to More Than Double Stores
items.summary: Asics Corp. plans to more than double its China store network and increase local production as the Japanese sportswear maker makes the country a key growth priority for 2027.

items.title: Review: UBS Group Sees Yuan Rising to 6.25 in Most Bullish Market Call
items.summary: UBS Group AG expects the yuan to strengthen toward 6.25 per dollar by the end of 2027, matching the market’s most bullish call yet on a currency that has outperformed most Asian peers this year.

items.title: Review: Skylark CFO Eyes US Expansion, More M&A
items.summary: Skylark, one of Japan’s largest restaurant chains, plans more M&A in 2027, and expects its growth-investment budget to match at least this year’s ¥50 billion ($314 million). CFO Yoshiaki Kita spoke to Bloomberg TV in Tokyo. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Review: Nvidia Has No Plans to Bring Back Jensen Huang
items.summary: As the former chief executive and his allies lobbied for his return, the company’s chair said the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as C.E.O.”

items.title: Review: After Days of Digital Outages, Americans Wonder if the Country Is Breaking
items.summary: The digital outages that began on Thursday may not be linked, but they have left Americans with a sense that the nation is off-kilter, with no one ready to fix it.

items.title: Review: Democrat Mary Peltola wins Alaska Senate race: AP projects
items.summary: Peltola's victory is the ninth Senate pickup for Democrats.
